messages:
omar: alert: seeing a sudden high-rate spike to /api/generate from hundreds of /24s, mostly HTTP/2, odd X-Client-Probe header. current RPS ~3k at edge-proxy. creating incident.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 created and assigned to @omar.
deploy-bot: Noted. Automated mitigation: enabling global short-term rate limit for /api/generate.
elisabeth: looks like a probing pattern — same header value repeated, likely traffic-smuggling probe. can we add a quick WAF header-block rule? :warning:
omar: applying WAF rule now. rule snippet: ```match: header['x-client-probe'] == '1' action: block id: tmp-7321```
marta: pushed IP block for top 20 offending /24s to edge ACLs. propagating to all regions.
kevin: adding token-level throttling to avoid collateral for legit users. provisional config: ```rate_limit: {scope: ip, requests_per_minute: 500, response_code: 429}```
ryan: watch out — we have a few enterprise customers in APAC that route through those ASN blocks. if they report issues we should have a rollback plan.
elisabeth: noted, pinging @support-team to open customer visibility notes and preempt messages to affected accounts.
support-team: creating customer bulletin draft, will coordinate with account owners.
sachin: metrics: after WAF+rate limits traffic dropped to ~250 RPS within 6m, error rate on /api/generate briefly rose to 4% (429s). no upstream resource exhaustion.
omar: rolling temporary mitigations for 2 hours, then evaluate. leaving block rule tmp-7321 and ACLs in place for now.
deploy-bot: WAF rule tmp-7321 active in all regions. edge ACLs synced.
kevin: follow-up: we should add an alert for sustained HTTP/2 connection spike pattern (more than 1k concurrent h2 streams with identical header fingerprint). I'll open an alert PR.
elisabeth: also add this probe signature to the WAF corpus and update the signatures repo.
marta: opening PR for runbook updates (incident response -> traffic abuse -> h2 probes). adding rollback instructions and customer-communication checklist.
sachin: post-incident summary: cause = traffic-smuggling probe via HTTP/2 with custom header; mitigations = WAF header match + edge ACLs + rate-limit; impact = transient increased 429s for heavy clients, no data exfiltration.
omar: post-incident actions: [1] persist signature + automation to convert tmp rules to managed signatures, [2] add alert for h2 fingerprint anomaly, [3] verify KMS/audit logs show all control-plane changes for the event, [4] run tabletop with support/account reps.
kevin: I'll handle KMS/audit log verification and share findings.
elisabeth: thanks all. keeping incident open until runbook PR and signature PR merged. great coordination. :thumbsup:
